page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the EIBSv5 server family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 112 dedicated vCPUs derived from 56 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1D cache per core. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.0 GB. The instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, but it is designed for high block storage performance and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. The multi-core stress-ng CPU test and Geekbench multi-core score both rank in the top 25%, supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 5839.55 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 335.8 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 25%, executing 96.47 million operations per second. Single-core performance, single-threaded compression, and small-model LLM inference speeds fall within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the E112ibs_v5 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that require isolated compute environments without the overhead of local physical disks. The lack of local storage is a tradeoff that necessitates reliance on external block storage, but the instance's high-performance block storage capabilities mitigate this. This server is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
